chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Dawud (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to show him a judgment from the judgments of the Hereafter. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Dawud! That which you asked Me, no one from My creation has been informed of it, nor is it befitting for anyone to judge by it other than Me.'

He said: So that did not prevent him from returning, so he asked Allah to show him a judgment from the judgments of the Hereafter. He said: So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: 'O Dawud! You have asked your Lord something which no prophet before you has asked. O Dawud! That which you asked, none from His creation has been informed of it, nor is it befitting for anyone to judge by it other than Him. Allah has answered your supplication and given you what you asked for. O Dawud! The first two litigants who come to you tomorrow, the judgment regarding them is from the judgments of the Hereafter.'

He said: So when Dawud (peace be upon him) morninged, he sat in his judicial council. An old man came to him, holding onto a youth, and with the youth was a bunch of grapes. So the old man said to him: 'O Prophet of Allah! This youth entered my garden and ruined my vineyard and ate from it without my permission, and this bunch he took without my permission.'

So Dawud said to the youth: 'What do you say?' So the youth confessed that he had done that. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Dawud! If I uncover for you from the judgments of the Hereafter, and you judge by it between the old man and the boy, your heart would not bear it and your people would not be pleased with it. O Dawud! Indeed, this old man stormed upon the father of this boy in his garden, so he killed him and usurped his garden and took from it forty thousand dirhams, so he buried them by the side of his garden. So hand a sword to the youth and order him to strike the neck of the old man, and hand over the garden to him and order him to dig in such and such a place and take his wealth.'

He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) was startled by that, and he gathered to him the scholars of his companions and informed them of the news, and he executed the judgment according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had revealed to him.

key_terms.أربعون ألف درهم: Forty thousand dirhams (a specific sum of wealth)
key_terms.اقتحم: To storm or break into forcefully

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet Dawud and the judgment of the Hereafter in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *al-Qada' al-Akhirah* (the Judgment of the Hereafter), where Prophet Dawud (AS) is granted divine insight into the hidden realities (*haqa'iq*) of a legal dispute. While the outward appearance (*zahir*) suggested the youth was at fault for eating grapes, the inner truth (*batin*) revealed the old man's usurpation of the youth's father and property, justifying a unique judicial ruling. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between literal justice and deeper, divinely revealed truth in prophetic judgment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Dawood<sup>as</sup> asked his<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Show him<sup>as</sup> a Judgement from the Judgements of the Hereafter. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! That which you<sup>as</sup> have asked Me<sup>azwj</sup>, no one from My<sup>azwj</sup> creatures has been notified of it, nor is it befitting for anyone that he judges by it, apart from Me<sup>azwj</sup>”.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So that did not prevent him<sup>as</sup> to repeat, so he<sup>as</sup> asked Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> Shows him<sup>as</sup> a Judgement from the Judgements of the Hereafter. So Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came over to him<sup>as</sup> and said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! You<sup>as</sup> have asked your<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> something which no Prophet<sup>as</sup> before you<sup>as</sup> has asked. O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! That which you asked, none from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures has been notified with, nor is it befitting for anyone that he<sup>as</sup> judged by it, apart from Him<sup>azwj</sup>. However, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Answered your<sup>as</sup> supplication, and has Granted you<sup>as</sup> what you<sup>as</sup> asked for. O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! The first two litigants who would intend to you tomorrow, judge regarding both of them from the Judgements of the Hereafter’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So when it was the morning, Dawood<sup>as</sup> sat is his<sup>as</sup> judicial council. An old man came over to him concerning a youth, and with him was the youth with a bunch of grapes. So the old man said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘O Prophet<sup>as</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! This youth entered my garden and spoilt my vineyard, and ate from it without my permission. And this is the bunch which he took without my permission’.

So Dawood<sup>as</sup> said to the youth: ‘What are you saying?’ So the youth confessed that he had done that. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! I<sup>azwj</sup> hereby Uncover for you<sup>as</sup> from the Judgements of the Hereafter. Therefore, judge by it between the old man and the boy. Your<sup>as</sup> heart, (however) would not be able to bear it, and your<sup>as</sup> people would not be pleased with it. O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! This old man stormed upon the father of this boy in his garden, so he killed him, and usurped his garden, and seized forty thousand Dirhams from it. So he buried it by the side of his garden. So hand a sword to the youth and order him that he should strike the neck of the old man, and hand over the garden to him, and order him that he should dig in such and such a place and take his wealth”.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Dawood<sup>as</sup> panicked from that and gathered to himself<sup>as</sup>, his<sup>as</sup> scholars, and his<sup>as</sup> companions, and informed them of the news, and passed the Judgement upon what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic had Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from abu Hamzah who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

once Dawud ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked his Lord to show him one of the cases of the next life being judged. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him revelation. It said, ‘O Dawud, what you have asked Me is something about which no one of My creatures has known. It is not proper for any of My creatures to judge in that manner besides Me.’

He (the Imam) said that this did not stop him from asking Allah to show him a case and judgment of the cases and judgments of the next life. He (the Imam) said that Jibril, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then came to him and said, ‘O Dawud, you had asked your Lord for something that no other Prophet before you had asked. What you have asked is not known to anyone of His creatures and it is not proper for anyone to judge in that manner besides Him. However, Allah has accepted your prayer and has granted what you wanted. O Dawud, the case of the first two parties that will come to you tomorrow, is one of the cases of the next life.’

He (the Imam) said that next day when Dawud ‘Alayhi al-Salam, took his seat in the adjudicating office, one old man who had grabbed a young boy with a bunch of grapes in his hand came to him. The old man said, £ 0 Prophet of Allah, this young man entered my garden, destroyed my vineyard, ate from them without my permission and this bunch is what he has taken without my permission.’

Dawud then asked the young man, ‘What do you say?’ The young man confessed that he has done so. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent revelation to Dawud and said, ‘If I reveal before you a case of the cases of the next life and you judge between the old man and the young man your heart cannot bear it and your people will not agree. O Dawud, this old man entered on the father of this boy in his garden and killed him, usurped his garden, took from him forty thousand dirham and buried it on the side of the garden. Therefore, you must give a sword to the young man and command him to strike the neck of the old man, give the garden back to him, command him to dig such and such place and take his assets thereof.

Dawud, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was shocked. He called the scholars of his companions, informed them of the news and then approved to issue the judgment as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, had revealed to him.’”
